subject.title: improve(setup): keep WSL operations inside the app-owned directory

question: Should SetupEngine preserve safe existing custom distro names while rejecting traversal, or intentionally narrow the custom-name contract and accept the documented residual filesystem race?
rationale: The patch changes an existing overrideable setup input and defines a residual security boundary, so automation cannot decide the permanent compatibility contract.

options.title: Preserve safe names
options.body: Retain containment and reparse-point checks, reject only path-dangerous names, document the contract, and require live WSL proof.

options.title: Adopt strict ASCII contract
options.body: Accept the compatibility break, document migration for custom configurations, and require live WSL proof before merge.

options.title: Pause boundary change
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers choose a stronger deletion design or a separately versioned strict mode.

recommendation.title: Preserve safe names
recommendation.body: Retain containment and reparse-point checks, reject only path-dangerous names, document the contract, and require live WSL proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest available public repository ownership signal for deciding a setup-wide compatibility and security contract.
